question.text: Consider a circle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mfenced><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>. If the circle touches the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> at the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math>, whose distance from the origin is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math> , then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is equal to _______.

solution.text:
Given: x-α2+y-β2=50

The given equation of circle represent centre as α,β and radius as 52 units.

Now, x+y=0 is tangent to the given circle at P.

We know that, radius is perpendicular to tangent at the point of tangency.

⇒CP⊥x+y=0 and CP=r

⇒r=α×1+β×112+12

⇒52=α+β2

⇒50=α+β22

⇒α+β2=100
